arguments.name: Scholars-on-scholars section is edifying
arguments.conclusion: Including scholars' comments about other scholars is worthwhile because it humanizes the debate and functions like mini book reviews.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: The section began as a personal list of post-1975 sources.
Comments by one respected scholar about another reveal their reasons and are often humorous.
Such material parallels the humanizing interpersonal details in The Chosen.

st1.quote: Look at that section as many book reviews. M I N I not M Y M I NI book reviews.

st2.quote: If you remember that this started out as a list only for me to update me on post 75 sources, I was curious when I'm just making something up.

st3.quote: If you go back and read Albert Fitzer's Quest of the Historical Jesus, read some of the things they say about each other.

st4.quote: It really humanizes these people and contextualizes them like, right?

st8.quote: Secondly, these guys, I respected them so much that when one of them goes off on another one, I want to know their reasons and why.

or1.quote: Look at that section as many book reviews. M I N I not M Y M I NI book reviews.
or1.why: No prior art is known to defend the inclusion of scholar-on-scholar commentary as an edifying feature of a resurrection survey volume; it is not a restatement of any standard resurrection argument.

or2.quote: If you go back and read Albert Fitzer's Quest of the Historical Jesus, read some of the things they say about each other.
or2.why: It brings the survey's own reception-history material (Fitzer, Strauss, Bultmann-era polemics) as evidence, which prior resurrection arguments do not use.

or3.quote: You know, in the movie now that's such a big hit, The Chosen, that's out right now, you get the apostles going off on each other.
or3.why: It connects modern popular-culture portrayal of the apostles to scholarly historiography, a cross-domain link the prior art does not make.

or4.why: No formalization, equation or model is offered.

arguments.weakest_link: The premise that such comments are 'like mini book reviews' is asserted rather than shown to carry evidential or scholarly value.
arguments.develop_next: Give a concrete example of a scholar-on-scholar comment that changed a substantive judgment (e.g., on Bultmann's body view), showing the section does real work.

arguments.name: Resurrection has practical theological significance
arguments.conclusion: The resurrection is practically significant because it grounds hope in death and shapes how believers live and spend their money.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: The New Testament links the resurrection of believers to Jesus's resurrection nearly twenty times.
Personal bereavement makes the hope of resurrection especially relevant.
If Jesus rose, the command to love others should affect practical decisions like finances.

st1.quote: So I think it really is practical.

st2.quote: And then the theological view that the theology that's linked to the resurrection New Testament more than any other is the resurrection of believers almost 20 times.

st3.quote: My sister-in-law just died and the the funeral was just days ago and my wife the mother of my four children died in 1995.

st4.quote: So how do you spend your money if that indeed is the second most important thing in your life?

st6.quote: So I think it really is practical.

st8.quote: I mean if those aren't the times when resurrection when you want to know if there's some hope there that's the time.

or1.quote: So how do you spend your money if that indeed is the second most important thing in your life?
or1.why: The hope-and-ethics link is a variant of Wright's resurrection-as-practical-eschatology argument, but Habermas ties it to his minimal-facts project and personal bereavement.

or2.quote: My sister-in-law just died and the the funeral was just days ago and my wife the mother of my four children died in 1995.
or2.why: It brings autobiographical bereavement experience and the 'almost 20 times' NT count as support, which the prior art does not use.

or3.quote: So how do you spend your money if that indeed is the second most important thing in your life?
or3.why: It connects resurrection belief to personal finance and the second greatest commandment, a practical bridge the prior art does not make.

or4.why: No formalization, equation or model is offered.

arguments.weakest_link: The step from 'the NT links resurrection of believers to Jesus's resurrection' to 'this is practically significant for you' needs the further premise that the NT linkage is true and normative.
arguments.develop_next: Cite the specific NT passages and their count so the 'almost 20 times' claim is checkable and the practical inference has a textual base.
